category: Vernacular funnel / CAC reduction (K-12 edtech app)
title: Vernacular WhatsApp demos cut a tier-2 edtech's CAC from ₹4,200 to ₹1,650 in Indore, Bhopal and Jabalpur
content: A K-12 learning-app startup sold an English-medium UI to Hindi-speaking parents across Indore, Bhopal and Jabalpur. Meta lead-gen ran at ₹38 CPL, but only 22% of leads showed up to a demo and just 6% of those went paid — real CAC ₹4,200 against a ₹5,999 annual plan, so payback never closed. Diagnosis: the buyer was the mother, who couldn't read the English onboarding and wouldn't trust an app she'd never heard of on Justdial. We rebuilt the funnel in Hindi. Meta creatives spoke parent-to-parent ('Aapke bachche ka result'), clicking to WhatsApp instead of a form. A Hindi-speaking counsellor sent a 90-second YouTube demo of the child's actual class, then a 7-day free trial on UPI autopay, plus a voice-note from a local 'topper ki maa'. Over 10 weeks CPL held at ₹41, but demo attendance jumped 22%→58% and demo-to-paid rose 6%→19%. CAC fell to ₹1,650; 14-day refund requests dropped 11%→4% because trust, not a discount, closed the sale, lifting annual-plan share.
lesson: In vernacular tier-2/3 markets the mother is the buyer, not the child who uses the app. Move the funnel off English forms onto WhatsApp plus a voice-note in her language, and sell trust — local proof and a real free trial — before price. Same ₹41 CPL, 3x the demo-to-paid rate, and refunds more than halved.
